features.summary: The Native package: NativeComponent, the base every Native declaration names, whose vendor is the DOM itself, the element the framework rendered, listened to by addEventListener and removeEventListener; and main's gather shorthand, which sends a member's input by an object-typed lambda and reads it by the name value whatever component the member binds. The rewrite keeps the base, sealed to ComponentVendor.Native, states once what a native event hands its listener, and sends a member by the input its bound component declares (N9.3, N14.4).

return self.Include(elementId, DefaultComponent.Vendor, bodyField, DefaultComponent.ValueMember, shape);
public sealed override ComponentVendor Vendor => ComponentVendor.Native;
public static ComponentVendor Native { get; } = new ComponentVendor(

NativeComponent is a Component (M12.N1) whose vendor is sealed to ComponentVendor.Native: the object is the element the render helper rendered, an empty path from it, and a listener subscribes by addEventListener and unsubscribes by removeEventListener, each a member lib.dom's EventTarget makes public (D17.3, D17.5).

A Native event hands its listener lib.dom's event object, an Event for change and a PointerEvent for click, whose target and currentTarget lib.dom types EventTarget | null; so each Native slice declares its event's payload as a class nested in the component that mirrors that lib.dom type with the members lib.dom types concretely, and no Target; a handler reads the component's own value through the component (M24.D1, probe:dom-change-listener-event, probe:dom-click-listener-event).

Each Native declaration mirrors the lib.dom interface of the element its render helper renders, HTMLInputElement, HTMLSelectElement, HTMLTextAreaElement or HTMLButtonElement, and names each member as that interface names it, so ALIS014 to ALIS020 check it as any declaration (N17.2); the check list mirrors the type its own browser code declares (M24.D2).

A request sends a member a Native input binds by the input its bound component declares, Input(r => r.Member, pipeline.Input(m => m.Member)), so a check box sends its Checked and a text box its Value, typed by the member (N9.3, N14.4, M7.N3).

meanings.meaning: A Native event hands its listener the lib.dom event object HTMLElementEventMap names for it, an Event for change and a PointerEvent for click (probe:dom-change-listener-event, probe:dom-click-listener-event), and the payload's declaration reads it at [0] (D17.4). Each Native slice declares that payload as a class nested in its component, named for the event (Changed, Clicked), which mirrors the lib.dom type, so ALIS016 checks each member against it (N17.2), as the owner's walk of the native text box built it (spec/NOTES.md:515, items 1 and 7). It declares the members lib.dom types concretely: Event's Type, IsTrusted and TimeStamp, and, on a click, each member PointerEvent, MouseEvent and UIEvent declare with a concrete type and no deprecation; it declares no Target, CurrentTarget, RelatedTarget or View, which lib.dom types EventTarget | null or Window | null (item 2). The event holds no value, so a handler reads the component's value from the component, through the rendered component or pipeline.Input(m => m.Member).Component<TComponent>() (N14.4, item 4); the DOM raises change after the value is committed, so the component holds what both lines' payload read. The input an Event<Changed> commits is ComponentInput.Of(value, committedBy: Change) as M7.N3 states it. A change the Native package's own code raises (the hidden field's, the radio group's) is a script's Event, whose IsTrusted reads false; a script's write raises no change on any Native input but the hidden field (M24.D3), as the DOM raises none.

features.oracle: lib.dom.d.ts of TypeScript 5.9.3 (node_modules/typescript/lib/lib.dom.d.ts in the main checkout): EventTarget's addEventListener and removeEventListener, Event's target and currentTarget typed EventTarget | null, and HTMLElementEventMap's change and click; and the browser, by the fact named (probe:dom-change-listener-event).

defects.defect: Main's Include(m => m.Member) names the member by an object-typed lambda, which ALIS009 refuses on the public surface, and reads the member's input by the name value whatever component it binds (Alis.Reactive.Native/Extensions/NativeGatherExtensions.cs:46 at 623dd4a27, its read written at Alis.Reactive/PlanAuthoring/Requests/GatherBuilder.cs:279-282 at 623dd4a27). A NativeCheckBox declares checked and value as a second name for it (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/BrowserObjects/BrowserObject.cs:198-204 at 623dd4a27), so the shorthand's value at the path value meets it in ObjectProperty.Merge, which throws where the view renders, "Property 'value' registered with path 'checked' but re-registered with path 'value'." (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/BrowserObjects/BrowserObjectContract.cs:343-346 at 623dd4a27). The rewrite sends a member by the input its bound component declares, typed by the member (N9.3, N14.4, M7.N3): the check box's Checked, and an object-typed lambda does not compile.

verdicts.reason: A vendor named by a string the runtime picks a driver by, native or fusion (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/browser-objects/component-driver.ts:89-90 at 623dd4a27), so the runtime names each vendor it serves. The rewrite carries the vendor as data the one driver follows (D17.3): ComponentVendor.Native, the element itself listened to by addEventListener and removeEventListener, which NativeComponent seals (M24.N1).

features.summary: NativeButton: a <button> under the id the developer chose, its text as textContent, focus and click, each lib.dom's HTMLButtonElement member by its name. Main spreads it over an events class, a payload class with no member, extensions that name textContent and focus by strings over ComponentRef, and a Reactive extension on the builder; the redesign declares it in one file with a click payload that holds no member. The rewrite keeps the redesign's members, mirrors lib.dom's HTMLButtonElement, and declares Click's payload as Clicked, nested in the component and mirroring lib.dom's PointerEvent, the type HTMLElementEventMap gives click (M24.D1, probe:dom-click-listener-event).

sentences.text: NativeButton mirrors lib.dom's HTMLButtonElement and declares TextContent as Property<string>, Element's textContent, which reads a string and takes null; Focus() as a method, HTMLElement's focus; and Click as Event<Clicked>, Clicked a class nested in it that mirrors lib.dom's PointerEvent, the type HTMLElementEventMap gives click, with Event's Type, IsTrusted and TimeStamp and each member PointerEvent, MouseEvent and UIEvent declare with a concrete type and no deprecation, AltKey, CtrlKey, ShiftKey and MetaKey, Button, Buttons, Detail, ClientX and the other coordinates, PointerId, PointerType and IsPrimary among them, never RelatedTarget or View, which lib.dom types EventTarget | null and Window | null (M24.D1, probe:dom-click-listener-event); each named as lib.dom names its public member.

Html.NativeButton(id, text) renders a <button> with the text under the id the developer chose, its type button unless Type says otherwise (N18.4); a button is no input, so no field renders it, and it binds no member.

features.summary: NativeCheckList: a list of check boxes bound to one member, its value the checked boxes' values, written, read and committed as one input, with options from CheckListItem or Option. Main renders an inline script that keeps a plain array on the container and a hidden comma list beside the boxes, so a write checks no box, and takes the radio group's item type; the redesign moves the value into the Native package's check list code, which checks the boxes a write names, and gives the list its own item. Both lines render the hidden comma list and name every box by the binding name, so a form's own submission sends each checked value twice. The rewrite keeps the redesign's members and its code's value and focus, declares the type that code defines, declares Change's payload as Changed, nested in the component and mirroring lib.dom's Event (M24.D1), and renders one carrier of the value by the member's kind, the code writing the joined text only where the list renders the hidden input (M24.D2).

sentences.text: NativeCheckList mirrors NativeCheckListElement, the type the Native package's check list code declares, an HTMLDivElement whose value is the checked boxes' values in the boxes' order, a list of text, and whose focus focuses the first box (M24.D2); it declares Value as Property<string[]>, Focus() and Change as Event<Changed>, Changed a class nested in it that mirrors lib.dom's Event, the type HTMLElementEventMap gives change, with Type, IsTrusted and TimeStamp (M24.D1), which each box raises and the list hears.

A NativeCheckList bound to a member is an input: its Value, committed by Change, is what a form sends and a check reads; a write of Value checks exactly the boxes whose values it holds, and a write of nothing checks none (M24.D2).

field.NativeCheckList() and field.NativeCheckList(build => ..) render the list under the field's id, a box per option from Items(IEnumerable<CheckListItem>) or Option(value), Option(value, text) and Option(value, text, description), each box checked as the member holds its value; a member whose JSON contract is a collection (D18.2) is sent by the boxes under its binding name, one entry per checked box, and a member of string by one hidden input that holds the checked values joined by commas, the boxes then nameless (M24.D2).
CheckListItem is the check list's own option, a value, a text and a description that is null when none is given; it is the check list's alone, and the radio group declares its own (M24.N7).

The rendered NativeCheckList's Reactive(c => c.Change, pipeline) handles its change from the plan's start; pipeline.Input(m => m.VisitDays).Component<NativeCheckList>() reaches it in any block (N14.4).

meanings.meaning: A check list's value is the checked boxes' values in the boxes' order. The Native package's check list code defines value and focus on the list's element on alis:mount and declares their type, NativeCheckListElement, an HTMLDivElement with value: string[], which the declaration mirrors (D17.5). A write checks exactly the boxes whose values it holds and unchecks the rest; a write of nothing checks none; a write raises no change, as a script's write to a box raises none. The render helper renders one carrier of the value for a form's own submission: a member whose JSON contract is a collection (D18.2) by the boxes, each under the binding name, so a submission holds one entry per checked box and none when none is checked; a member of string by one hidden input under the binding name that holds the checked values joined by commas, with the boxes nameless; the code writes the joined text on each change and write where the list renders that input, and writes none where it renders none. A request the framework sends writes the list's Value in its wire form either way (D9.15).
